Whiten an RGB Hex Value

Source: R/lighten_hex.R
lighten_hex.Rd

lighten_hex() whitens an RGB hex value to be some proportion of its original value.

Usage

lighten_hex(hex, p)

Arguments

hex

a valid RGB hex value, with leading pound sign (#)

p

some value between 0 and 1 for whitening the RGB hex value in question.

Value

lighten_hex() takes an RGB hex value and a value between (and including) 0 and 1 and returns a HEX code that retains some proportion (p) of its original value. For example, lighten_hex("#000000", 0) takes the RGB hex value for pure black and whitens it to retain none of its original color. This would be white. Alternatively, lighten_hex("#002f5f", .8) takes the color corresponding with Stockholm University Blue (g_c("su_blue")) and whitens it to retain 80% of its original value. This procedure closely approximates what Stockholm University presents as 80% of its original color (#32587E compared to #33587f it presents on its website).

Details

This function is mostly for internal use, but you're welcome to experiment with it.

Author

Steven V. Miller

Examples


lighten_hex(g_c("su_fire"), .7)
#> [1] "#F19B66"
# Compare with...
g_c("su_fire70")
#> [1] "#f19b66"
